CVE-2016-3739.patch_commit_message:
mbedtls/polarssl: set "hostname" unconditionally

...as otherwise the TLS libs will skip the CN/SAN check and just allow
connection to any server. curl previously skipped this function when SNI
wasn't used or when connecting to an IP address specified host.

CVE-2016-3739

Bug: https://curl.haxx.se/docs/adv_20160518A.html
Reported-by: Moti Avrahami

new_lines: /* mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname() sets the name to use in CN/SAN checks *and*
the name to set in the SNI extension. So even if curl connects to a
host specified as an IP address, this function must be used. */
/* ssl_set_hostname() sets the name to use in CN/SAN checks *and* the name
to set in the SNI extension. So even if curl connects to a host
specified as an IP address, this function must be used. */

behavior_changes: Previously, mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname (or ssl_set_hostname) was only called if the host was not an IP address and SNI was enabled; on failure, a warning was logged but the connection continued.
After patch, the hostname-setting function is called unconditionally; if it fails, the function immediately returns CURLE_SSL_CONNECT_ERROR.
The removal of the pre‑conditions (IP check, SNI flag) ensures hostname verification is always performed by the TLS library.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Mandatory server identity verification through TLS hostname (CN/SAN) checks for all connections.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch ensures the hostname is unconditionally passed to the TLS library via mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname / ssl_set_hostname, enabling certificate CN/SAN checks even for IP addresses and SSLv3 connections. It also hardens error handling by converting a warning into a fatal error if the hostname cannot be set.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The pre-patch code conditionally called the TLS hostname-setting function (mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname / ssl_set_hostname) only when SNI was enabled and the host was not a numerical IP address. Because this function also enables certificate hostname verification (CN/SAN checks), skipping it allowed connections to proceed without verifying the server's certificate against the expected hostname, enabling MITM attacks with any valid certificate.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Conditional invocation of the hostname-setting API based on SNI usage and IP address detection, leading to omission of mandatory certificate hostname verification.

CVE-2016-3739.vulnerability_description: The (1) mbed_connect_step1 function in lib/vtls/mbedtls.c and (2) polarssl_connect_step1 function in lib/vtls/polarssl.c in cURL and libcurl before 7.49.0, when using SSLv3 or making a TLS connection to a URL that uses a numerical IP address, allow remote attackers to spoof servers via an arbitrary valid certificate.

CVE-2017-9502.patch_commit_message:
url: fix buffer overwrite with file protocol (CVE-2017-9502)

Bug: https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/1540
Advisory: https://curl.haxx.se/docs/adv_20170614.html

Assisted-by: Ray Satiro
Reported-by: Marcel Raad

new_lines: /* only file: is allowed to omit one or both slashes */
old_lines: size_t urllen = strlen(data->change.url); /* original URL length */

behavior_changes: Prefixlen is now validated against the original URL before incrementing; if the URL does not start with the expected protocol, parsing fails with CURLE_URL_MALFORMAT.
The addition for the '://' sequence is conditional on its actual presence; for file: URLs, prefixlen is increased by 1 or 2 based on whether a single slash follows 'file:'.
The reurl allocation size is changed from 'urllen + 2' to 'prefixlen + plen + 1', eliminating the mismatch between allocation and written data.
In the file URL handling block, *prot_missing is explicitly set to !url_has_scheme, ensuring correct state for subsequent prefix calculations.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Bounds-safe heap allocation for URL reconstruction that matches the exact byte counts derived from the actual URL contents.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch validates that the actual URL prefix matches the expected protocol and slashes before adjusting prefixlen, adds a special case for file: where slashes may be partially omitted, and replaces the allocation expression with the exact required size (prefixlen+plen+1) to prevent buffer overflow.

root_cause_analysis.summary: In parseurlandfillconn, when the URL scheme is present, the prefixlen calculation unconditionally added strlen(protop)+strlen("://") without verifying that the URL actually contains those bytes. For file: URLs lacking two slashes (e.g., 'file:c:/path'), prefixlen was overestimated by up to 7 bytes, causing the rebuilt URL allocation (urllen+2) to be too small for the actual concatenation (prefixlen+plen+1), resulting in a heap buffer overflow during the memcpy of the path.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Unconditional addition of strlen(protop)+3 to prefixlen in the !*prot_missing branch, combined with allocation based on the original URL length (urllen+2) rather than the actual required size (prefixlen+plen+1).

CVE-2017-9502.vulnerability_description: In curl before 7.54.1 on Windows and DOS, libcurl's default protocol function, which is the logic that allows an application to set which protocol libcurl should attempt to use when given a URL without a scheme part, had a flaw that could lead to it overwriting a heap based memory buffer with seven bytes. If the default protocol is specified to be FILE or a file: URL lacks two slashes, the given "URL" starts with a drive letter, and libcurl is built for Windows or DOS, then libcurl would copy the path 7 bytes off, so that the end of the given path would write beyond the malloc buffer (7 bytes being the length in bytes of the ascii string "file://").

CVE-2019-5481.patch_commit_message:
security:read_data fix bad realloc()

... that could end up a double-free

CVE-2019-5481
Bug: https://curl.haxx.se/docs/CVE-2019-5481.html

behavior_changes: Removed the temporary `tmp` pointer and always updates `buf->data` directly.
Now the error condition checks `!len || !buf->data` instead of only `tmp == NULL`, handling both zero-length reads and reallocation failures.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Memory safety – no dangling pointers after reallocation that could cause double-free.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: Always assign `buf->data` to the `Curl_saferealloc()` return value and correctly check for allocation failure by testing both a zero length and a null pointer.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The `read_data` function fails to update `buf->data` to the pointer returned by a successful `Curl_saferealloc()`, leaving it dangling and leading to a double-free when later freed.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: After calling `tmp = Curl_saferealloc(buf->data, len)`, the old code only assigned `buf->data = tmp` when `tmp == NULL`; on success (non-NULL), `buf->data` continued pointing to the already-freed old buffer, causing a double-free on subsequent deallocation.
